def: A type whose value is one of several types and that records which one it currently is (also called a tagged union). The standard implementation in C++ is `std::variant`.

Each type in the template arguments `Types` of `variant<Types...>`; when a variant holds a value, the type of that value must be one of them. The same type may appear more than once, in which case only indices can distinguish them.

The state in which a `variant` holds no value: `valueless_by_exception()` is true and `index()` is `variant_npos`. It arises only when initialization of the new value throws an exception during a type-changing assignment or `emplace`.

A design trade-off of `std::variant`: the contained value must be nested within the object (no heap allocation), so the strong never-empty guarantee is not provided; in normal use it always holds a value, and it may enter the valueless state only when an exception interrupts a type switch.

The expository device used by variant's converting constructor/converting assignment to choose the stored type: an `FUN(T_i)` is constructed for each candidate type for which `T_i x[] = {std::forward<T>(t)};` is well-formed (i.e. not narrowing), overload resolution is performed for `FUN(std::forward<T>(t))`, and the selected `T_j` is the stored type.

An exposition-only function template in the specification of `std::visit` that accepts the four reference forms of `variant<Ts...>` and returns them unchanged; through template argument deduction it lets a class uniquely derived from a variant specialization also be visited by `visit` (C++23, P2162R2).

The idiom `template<class... Ts> struct overloaded : Ts... { using Ts::operator()...; };`: multiply inherit from several lambdas and merge their `operator()`s into one overload set with a using pack expansion, commonly used as a visitor for `std::visit`; since C++20 aggregate CTAD makes a deduction guide unnecessary.
The term used in [any]: a type that can hold values of different types, remembers the type of the value, but performs no conversions between types, such as `std::any`.
